notes: The update notice now works the way it always said it did. There was no repeating check at all: a radio left open asked once, at launch, and then reported that one answer as "Up to date" for as long as the window stayed open -- which is the case the six-hour interval was chosen for. And the launch check itself waited out those six hours, so a machine that had asked in the morning went on saying "Up to date" all day, through any number of relaunches. Opening the radio now asks unless it asked in the last ten minutes, and a repeat runs every six hours while it is open. The dot at the head of the pill blinks: lit for three quarters of every two seconds, snapping on and fading off over sixty milliseconds. The pill itself fades in over the same sixty. A machine set to reduced motion gets both held still. Two controls that were meant to be hidden were drawn on every machine, because a class rule setting display beats the hidden attribute: Open app folder sat permanently beside Reset to defaults instead of appearing only while Shift is held, and the reduced-motion scrolling switch was offered to everyone rather than only to machines that ask for reduced motion. The Start menu entry is now called "Deskside Radio - Update" rather than "Update Deskside Radio", because an alphabetical All apps list filed the old name under U, where nobody looking for their radio thinks to look. The old entry is removed once the new one is written. And the line in Settings that tells you how to take an update now names the file in the app folder first, with the Start menu second: the file ships inside the zip, so it is there however the folder arrived, while the Start menu entry only exists where the installer made one. Unzipping by hand used to leave the app naming something that had never been created. And taking an update is now one link rather than three routes to choose between. The notice in Settings offers Download the updater, which is the same file the release page hands a first-time installer -- with no index.html beside it, and there is none in a Downloads folder, it goes to the folder it installed to. Installing and updating stop being two procedures to remember. The copy already in the app folder still works and still costs no security prompts, and the readme says so, but it is no longer in the one line somebody reads when they want the new version and nothing else. Two faults in the installer, both found by following its own instructions. Unzipping the archive and running the script inside it installed the radio into the folder it was unzipped into -- Downloads, usually -- with the Desktop shortcut and the Start menu entry both pointing there. The rule was "index.html is beside me, so I am inside an install", and an unpacked archive has exactly that shape, because the installer ships inside the zip. An install now carries assets/installed-here.txt, which the zip never does, and that is what tells the two apart; an unzipped folder is recognised, left alone, and told so before anything is written. Separately, downloading the installer and running it with a perfectly good install already in place was refused outright, with a message explaining an index.html check the code never made -- which is the exact route the app now recommends. An install at the target is an update, wherever the script was run from.
